title: Voter Backlash as Mayor Petra Flip-Flops on Rival's Competence - NewsBreak
text:
5 hours ago Jim Petra, Mayor of Cleveland Heights Photo by Cleveland Heights, Public Image Cleveland Heights, OH. It's the race for the Ohio House District 18 position. As some voters are voting early, others are going to the polls to decide whom to vote for.
In Cleveland Heights, it appears to be another drama-filled story of a labor organizer - the bus driver for South Euclid, Davida Russell, seeking the position along with Gabe Crenshaw, Cleveland Heights School and University Heights School Board President, Peter Hoffman, Retired Professional, and Sean Grube.
What concerns are weighing on the minds of voters in Cleveland Heights? Why are residents expressing their dissatisfaction with Mayor Jum Petras and the members of the Cleveland Heights City Council? It's time to examine these pressing issues and hold our leaders accountable.
During last year's Mayoral Race, Russell was Petras' opponent, and voters were uncertain about who would ultimately win. As the competition intensified, Petras accused Russell of lying, claiming that she misrepresented her educational background in his campaign materials. Russell stated that she graduated from Cleveland State University, but that was later found to be false. A dditionally, she claimed to be the endorsed Democrat, a statement that was also untrue.
Postcard from Jim Petras, Mayor, Cleveland Heights, OH Photo by The Brown Report Newspaper A month ago, Russell made a false claim about giving every business in Cleveland Heights one million dollars. We investigated the assertion and found it to be a lie .
"I don't like liars. I know that candidates do not tell the truth - especially politicians. These falsehoods are ridiculous. I am evenly bothered by Mayor Petra. First, he tells us in so many words that this lady is not fit to serve in a government capacity, and now he supports her. Something is wrong with him. Now, I don't trust him. I will not be supporting them in the future. These people can't be trusted. I hope that all the voters in Cleveland Heights see through this mess with him and her," said H. Robinson, a Cleveland Heights senior.
Petra told voters that Davida Russell Does Not Tell the Truth, and that she had the worst attendance record Petra mentioned in his campaign mailer that Russell has the support of the Cuyahoga County Republican Party. He highlighted that less than 10% of her contributions came from Cleveland Heights. In comparison, over 50% came from special-interest groups in the Columbus area and Washington, D.C. Additionally, he noted that she had the worst attendance record of any Council member over the past decade.
"Aren't special interest groups considered dark money?" asked Ms. Robinson. "If she is a Democrat, why is she being supported by Republicans? Is she a fan of Donald Trump, or is she one of those closet Republicans? This situation makes me sick. It's the reason I don't want to get involved in this mess. I supported Mayor Petra because of what he told us about that woman, Davida. Now, people are telling me that he supports her? Why would he support someone who aligns with Trump and everything he is doing, especially to the black community? Why would she be in cahoots with him?" I will not give her my vote, and I will no longer support our mayor. Thank God I have other candidates to consider," added Ms. Robinson.
Election day is Tuesday, May 5, 2026. Polls open at 6:30 pm. For more information about Election 2026, voters can contact the Board of Elections .
